summary: SUNation Energy filed an 8-K disclosing a First Amendment to its June 5, 2026 merger agreement whereby wholly owned Merger Sub will merge into Suniva, Inc., leaving Suniva as a wholly owned SUNation subsidiary. The amendment, dated September 4, 2026, permits Suniva warrant exchanges for SUNation securities, adds stockholder approvals for an authorized share increase from 1 billion to 1.5 billion and lender-security issuances, eases the closing net cash requirement to negative $2.5 million, and allows a $500,000 tail-insurance escrow. SUNation will seek up to $2,608,303 of related-party loan repayments or conversions at $2.26 per share. No price, premium, or board recommendation is stated. Watch for stockholder approval risk and the regulatory clock.
